history.dynasty: Not documented (founded by Ganga Ram Barooah)
history.period: c. 19th century (first structure 150+ years old; renovated in 1966)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: this temple is at Rajaduar in NORTH GUWAHATI on the north bank of the Brahmaputra, NOT in Dispur. Documented with the corrected location. The Doul Govinda Temple stands at the foothills of Chandra Bharati hill, devoted to Lord Krishna (Govinda); 'Doul' is the local name for the Holi festival, in which the Krishna idol is swung on a decorated Doul (swing) for five days in Phalguna (Feb-Mar), the temple's signature event drawing ~5,000 pilgrims. Legend: a milch cow would wander to a patch of birina grass in the Sandhya-Jhar woods near Jekeria (Rangia subdivision) and pour milk over it; when Ganga Ram Barooah had the spot dug, an idol of Krishna playing the flute was found and installed here. The first structure went up over 150 years ago and was rebuilt through public donations in 1966. A Vaishnavite shrine with a Namghar (prayer hall) in the same premises, where Mangala Aarti, bhog and Sandhya Aarti are offered daily.

name: Doul Govinda Temple
town_description: North Guwahati is a historic town on the north bank of the Brahmaputra in Kamrup Metropolitan district, facing Guwahati city across the river. It is known for its cluster of old temples - Doul Govinda, Dirgheshwari, Aswaklanta, Rudreswar - and the IIT Guwahati campus at Amingaon; the temple is reached by ferry from Fancy Bazaar Ghat to Rajaduar.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport (Guwahati) - about 25 km.
travel.railway: Guwahati Railway Station - nearest railhead; the temple is reached by ferry from Fancy Bazaar Ghat to Rajaduar (5-minute walk after landing).
travel.road: Ferries and steamers run from Fancy Bazaar Ghat to Rajaduar (easiest, fastest); trekkers/buses from Kharguli, Adabari and Jalukbari in Guwahati (verify exact services).

visitor_information.best_time: November to April (river cruise and Brahmaputra beach walks best in this window); Holi (Feb-Mar) for the five-day Doul Utsav.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Doors open ~7:00 AM; closed during afternoon hours; evening aarti with kirtan; sources disagree on exact morning/afternoon/evening slots (verify).
